commit_scope: Implementation, CPU regressions and launch runbook are in 4f8bab9f. This regenerated readiness record is committed separately.

blockers_addressed.summary: Wrapper cancellation released admission while its actual SSH/SCP child remained alive
blockers_addressed.fix: Publish a durable active reservation before creating a local session supervisor. The supervisor watches the wrapper, terminates/reaps the owned session on cancellation, wrapper death or deadline expiry, and only then clears the reservation. Gate.claim checks this reservation even after the wrapper OS lock is gone. POSIX session process groups isolate cancellation from the shared persistent master.
blockers_addressed.timeout_fix: Use one end-to-end execution deadline across wrapper startup, gate admission, master setup, rate spacing and command execution. cpuV RPC callers wait for supervised cleanup instead of racing it with an equal outer timeout.
regressions: test_real_wrapper_cancellation_keeps_gate_until_session_reaped: terminate, kill and timeout cancellation, each for commands and transfers, with real local children
test_actual_subprocess_outer_timeout_reaps_owned_local_session: actual subprocess.run outer timeout and kill/communicate behavior
test_real_rpc_deadline_allows_inner_cleanup_and_never_replays: both ops.remote and cpus_checking.rpc with real local wrapper/supervisor/session processes

implementation.control_master: yes for the persistent master, no for sessions
implementation.shared_pool_scope: All agents/worktrees using the same Linux/WSL client and OS user; independent of arm, run and PID
implementation.missing_master_fallback: ProxyCommand=false prevents a session from silently opening a direct connection
implementation.session_cleanup: Independent local supervisor monitors wrapper lifetime and execution deadline; terminates the owned session/group, waits up to one second before escalation on POSIX, and reaps before clearing admission
implementation.abrupt_supervisor_or_launch_failure: Durable active.json remains; subsequent callers fail closed with bounded admission wait. Documented operator recovery requires verifying all owned session processes have exited; no age/PID-only automatic clearing.
implementation.platform: Linux/WSL OpenSSH; native Windows fails before starting SSH. Windows process supervision is exercised with local Python children only.

api.command: command(host, remote_command, timeout=None, legacy=None) -> supervised/gated subprocess argv for cpuV, including an absolute monotonic deadline for finite budgets; original argv for other hosts
api.rsync_shell: rsync_shell(host) -> remote-shell command string using the same supervised pool for cpuV
api.Gate.claim: Gate(directory).claim(deadline=None) -> context manager; OS lock plus durable active-session exclusion
api.Gate.admit: gate.admit(deadline=None), under claim; persisted attempt spacing and bounded waiting
api.cli: python -B -m tools.coopmwm.cpuv_ssh [--timeout SECONDS] run -- 'COMMAND' | put LOCAL ABSOLUTE_REMOTE | get LOCAL ABSOLUTE_REMOTE | rsh cpuV COMMAND...
api.timeouts: CLI default 180 end-to-end execution seconds; 0 inherits caller lifetime. Cleanup can extend return beyond the execution deadline. cpuV RPC outer timeouts are disabled because the supervised inner deadline includes setup/admission and must finish cleanup; external wrapper termination is independently supervised.
api.python_script_remote_calls: tools.coopbandit.ops.remote automatically routes cpuV; caller binds PYTHON['cpuV'] to the qualified interpreter
integrations: tools/coopbandit/ops.py shared remote operations used by tools.coopmwm.ops.ssh
tools/coopmwm/cpus_checking.py configurable RPC and both rsync transfers
